did_you_know.text: Did you know? Chapter 1 describes Ahasuerus as king over 127 provinces, from India to Cush—a description emphasizing the extent of his kingdom according to the account in the scroll.
Did you know? Ahasuerus’s royal headquarters were in Susa, the capital, where he sat on his royal throne.
Did you know? Ahasuerus’s first banquet lasted 180 days, during which the king displayed the wealth of his kingdom and the splendor of his greatness.
Did you know? After the lengthy banquet, Ahasuerus held another banquet for the people of Susa, from the greatest to the least, lasting seven days.
Did you know? At the banquet, it was decreed that no one would be forced to drink: each person could drink as he wished, according to the king’s order.
Did you know? At the same time, Queen Vashti held a separate banquet for the women in the royal palace of Ahasuerus.
Did you know? When Vashti refused to come before the king at his command, Ahasuerus became extremely angry, and his fury burned within him.
Did you know? Ahasuerus consulted seven senior officials of Persia and Media, who were regarded as the foremost men in the kingdom and as those who saw the king’s face.
Did you know? Memucan proposed that a law be established that Vashti would never again appear before the king and that her royal position would be given to another woman.

Did you know? The royal decree was sent to every province of the kingdom, to each people in its own language, declaring that every man should rule his own household and speak the language of his people.
